rationale: B wins by a nose because it gives the founder more usable rooms to enter: investor thesis, captive-market pressure, disclosure gap, category trend, and payroll complexity. A's sharpest line, "The number Toast won't give you: default rates on its restaurant cash advances," is real, but the set gets too narrow and throws payroll away as a duplicate when it is clearly a separate workforce/software story. B's "How your point-of-sale vendor became your lender — and what restaurant owners can't easily do about it" has the stronger conflict, even though it needs proof before that switching-friction claim can stand upright.
gaps_in_A: "The prevailing belief is that a newly profitable, publicly traded platform lending against its own customers' sales has a clean, well-understood book" invents a straw-man market belief. The disclosure gap is enough; do not decorate it.
"Toast payroll solves the tipped-vs-hourly staffing headache" is refused as a duplicate, but payroll is not lending. A missed a distinct HR/workforce angle sitting in the update.
"there is no live news signal in this update" is too dismissive. The bundling, 120,000-location milestone, and recent profitability are weak-to-medium pegs, not nothing.
The first and third angles both circle the same public-market fintech-margin story, so the set is more disciplined than B but thinner than it looks.
gaps_in_B: "opting out of its financial products comes with real friction" is plausible, but the update does not prove it. That belongs in required proof, not the headline logic.
"Fee complaints are on record" overstates the fact block. The update says some owners complained; it does not establish documented complaints, volume, venue, or pattern.

"Toast tells investors hardware is low-margin" and "explicit management framing" add investor-relations specificity the update did not provide. The safer claim is that Toast says fintech is higher-margin than hardware.
The payroll angle imports unsupported detail like "tipped minimum wage variation by state, tip pooling rules, tip credits." Relevant, yes; grounded in the update, no.
